module_title: Municipalities - Constitutional Provisions, Reservations, and Planning Committees
introduction: At this level, we dive into the specific constitutional articles (Part IX-A: Articles 243P to 243ZG), the rules for reservations, and the crucial planning committees established to bridge the gap between rural and urban development.

core_concepts.title: Reservation of Seats (Article 243T)
core_concepts.description: Seats are reserved for SCs and STs in proportion to their population. Additionally, not less than one-third (1/3rd) of the total seats must be reserved for women (including women from SC/ST categories).

core_concepts.title: Wards Committees (Article 243S)
core_concepts.description: There shall be constituted Wards Committees consisting of one or more wards within the territorial area of a municipality having a population of 3 lakh or more.

core_concepts.title: District Planning Committee - DPC (Article 243ZD)
core_concepts.description: Every state must constitute a DPC at the district level. Its job is to consolidate the plans prepared by the Panchayats AND the Municipalities in the district and prepare a draft development plan for the district as a whole.

core_concepts.title: Metropolitan Planning Committee - MPC (Article 243ZE)
core_concepts.description: Every metropolitan area (having a population of 10 lakh or more) must have an MPC to prepare a draft development plan for the entire metropolitan area.

important_entities.name: State Election Commission (Article 243ZA)
important_entities.significance: The superintendence, direction, and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to the municipalities are vested in the State Election Commission (not the Election Commission of India).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A District Planning Committee (DPC) combines plans for both Rural and Urban areas in a district. A Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC) is only for large urban agglomerations (population > 10 Lakh).
Just like in Panchayats, providing reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in municipalities is NOT mandatory. It is left to the discretion of the State Legislature.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Z-D for District, Z-E for mEtropolitan
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Article 243ZD is for District Planning Committee. Article 243ZE is for Metropolitan Planning Committee.

exam_strategy_tips: The population threshold for creating a Wards Committee (3 Lakhs) and a Metropolitan area (10 Lakhs) are highly tested facts.
Remember that the State Finance Commission (Article 243Y) reviews the financial position of both Panchayats and Municipalities.
